title: Alternator

introduction.definition: An alternator is a synchronous AC generator. A DC-excited rotor (here 4 salient poles) turns inside a 3-phase stator winding; its moving magnetic field induces AC voltage. A brushless exciter with rotating diodes supplies the field current, controlled by the AVR.
introduction.summary: An alternator (synchronous AC generator) produces alternating current when its rotor field turns inside the stator winding. In a brushless design a small exciter on the same shaft generates AC that rotating diodes rectify to feed the main rotor poles — no brushes or slip rings. The AVR adjusts the exciter field to hold the output voltage constant.

magnetic_field.title: Rotating magnetic field
magnetic_field.description: DC in the field coils makes the rotor poles alternately N and S. As the rotor turns, this field sweeps past the stator conductors and induces a 3-phase AC voltage. Frequency = poles × rpm / 120 (4 poles at 1500 rpm → 50 Hz).

annotations.text: Flux crosses the air gap pole → stator → next pole

foundation: Mount on a rigid, level foundation or grouted baseplate sized for the machine mass and dynamic loads (typically ≥3–5 × machine mass for reciprocating machines).
Check for soft foot before final bolting.
alignment: Align driver and driven shafts with a laser or dial-indicator method to the coupling maker's tolerances; re-check hot alignment where thermal growth is significant.
piping: Cable termination sized for rated current; earthing of frame and neutral per system design.
commissioning: Check rotation direction with the coupling disconnected.
Fill lubricant to the correct level and grade.
Start unloaded where possible; record vibration, temperatures, current and pressures as a baseline.

causes: Failed diode, AVR fault, loss of residual magnetism

script.narration: This module introduces the Alternator.
An alternator is a synchronous AC generator.
A DC-excited rotor (here 4 salient poles) turns inside a 3-phase stator winding; its moving magnetic field induces AC voltage.
A brushless exciter with rotating diodes supplies the field current, controlled by the AVR.
Typical applications include diesel and gas generating sets; hydro and steam turbine generators; marine and rail power; wind turbines (synchronous types).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Alternator – Rotor: 4 Salient Poles with Field Coils, Exciter Armature & Rotating Rectifier.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.

video_tutorials.title: Alternator — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Alternator.
Check voltage, current balance, temperatures.
Insulation resistance / polarisation index test.
Test rotating diodes.
Clean windings, replace bearings.
Watch for loss of voltage: no output. Common cause: failed diode, avr fault, loss of residual magnetism.
Watch for winding insulation failure: earth fault trip. Common cause: moisture, overheating, ageing.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
